newsitem.title: USA: Albany, N.Y., seeks smaller tax increase - paper.
newsitem.headline: Albany, N.Y., seeks smaller tax increase - paper.

text.p: Albany, N.Y.'s Board of Education said it hoped to present residents with a budget that raised taxes less than the seven percent increase approved last year, the Albany Times Union reported on Sunday.
The paper quoted the associate superintendent as saying specific figures for the 1997-98 budget were not yet available.
Last year, Albany board members fought bitterly before approving a $92 million compromise plan.

The board's three contracts with unions, teachers, clerical staff and administrators, expire this year, but the local officials said they hoped to get more state aid, and could get another $500,000 through federal Medicaid funds for special education.
The board will get the spending plan on March 14, approve a budget on April 15, and must hold a public hearing on April 29, before the public vote slated for May 14.
